transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (CSM), Liam (SE), Samantha (VP Eng), Andre (CTO), Maya (Platform)

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, really excited to kick off, um this should be a fairly structured 45ish minute kickoff, then we'll leave time for q's and any deep technical items, priya and liam from our team are here.
00:12 Samantha: thanks jordan, yeah excited to get started, we've got a couple goals for this call — align on timeline, security, and a simple plan to run a pilot.
00:24 Jordan: perfect, I'll run through the onboarding plan, then priya will cover success/ops, liam will handle the technical checklist and benchmarking plan. quick round robin intro?
00:35 Andre: andrew — actually Andre here, CTO, we'll own infra and signing off on security.
00:41 Maya: maya, platform eng, i'll be setting up VPC peering and service accounts.
00:47 Priya: i'll be CSM, own the onboarding cadence and stakeholder comms.
00:52 Liam: liam, solutions eng, i'll run the bench and help with model selection/tuning.
00:59 Jordan: ok first up: goals. cypress wants to run clinical triage LLMs in production with predictable latency and cost, and data residency constraints for PHI. success criteria captured as: p95 latency under 200ms for single-turn gen, end-to-end cost target per 1k requests, and SOC2 compliance. does that look right?
01:17 Samantha: yes that's right. also want an audit log for every inference and ability to rotate keys (kms) per our policy.
01:26 Priya: noted - we'll make sure security docs cover audit logs and KMS integrations.
01:30 Jordan: cool, high level onboarding timeline: week 1 - access and network setup, week 2 - pilot run and initial benchmarks, week 3 - iterate on model/quantization settings and run durability tests, week 4 - rollout plan for production. flexible of course.
01:45 Samantha: timeline works. are you recommending hosted or dedicated for initial pilot?
01:50 Liam: good question, from the SE perspective for a health workload i'd advise starting with Redwood Dedicated reserved pool for predictable latency and to isolate PHI traffic — but we can do an initial hosted pilot if you want faster time-to-value. tradeoffs are isolation and SLA vs speed of setup.
02:08 Andre: curious about private deployment for stricter compliance — we have on-prem requirements for some clients. how heavy is that setup?
02:16 Jordan: private is definitely supported (Redwood Private), it's more of a multi-week project — needs private control plane and usually a support engagement. for most customers Dedicated + VPC peering covers compliance.
02:28 Maya: if we do dedicated + VPC peering, what about egress? we need no public internet for model uploads.
02:35 Liam: we support private egress routes and S3 bucket access via VPC endpoints. small config on your side to allow buckets and control plane connectivity. we'll include a configuration doc.
02:48 Samantha: ok good. then dedicated + VPC peering likely what we want for pilot.
02:53 Jordan: noted. next: security and compliance checklist. priya, you want to run through docs we'll share?
02:59 Priya: sure, we'll share SOC 2 attestation, our ISO summary, data retention defaults, and the security FAQ. items you'll need to confirm: SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC roles for team, encryption at rest (KMS), audit log access, and contract/data processing addendum.
03:20 Andre: SAML + SCIM is required. we use Okta.
03:24 Priya: great, we'll include the SSO integration steps.
03:27 Maya: about keys — we want customer-managed keys (CMK) if possible.
03:31 Liam: yes we integrate with KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated; hosted also supports BYOK via keystore in most regions. i'll follow up with integration notes.
03:42 Jordan: now let's cover pilot scope. recommended start with two flows: 1) clinical triage short prompts (single-turn), and 2) longer multi-turn patient follow-ups (chat-like). we'll measure latency (p50/p95), token cost, and quality regressions.
03:58 Samantha: sample traffic is 3k requests/day for first month, spiky up to 20 reqs/sec during peak, average prompt length is 120 tokens, response 180 tokens.
04:12 Liam: that helps; for those numbers we'll show batching suggestions but maintain latency SLO; we might recommend quantized models for cost savings if quality holds.
04:23 Andre: can you explain quantization tradeoffs quickly?
04:26 Liam: sure — quantization reduces model size and memory footprint, can reduce latency on some hardware, but may introduce small accuracy regressions. we'll run evals on your prompts to validate. sometimes 8-bit works well; sometimes 4-bit with special kernels.
04:41 Samantha: ok want to see the evals.
04:44 Jordan: we'll set up an eval harness, share prompt set, and run it in week 2.
04:49 Speaker 1: (inaudible)
04:52 Maya: networking nuts and bolts — what info do you need from us?
04:55 Liam: primarily VPC CIDR, AWS account id for peering, list of allowed S3 buckets, and IAM role details. we'll send a template.
05:05 Maya: we'll get that to you by monday.
05:08 Priya: noted in action items.
05:10 Jordan: ok next, data residency and retention — cypress needs logs for 7 years for audit, but we can store full audit logs and token metadata; raw model I/O containing PHI is configurable for retention. we'll include options in the DPA.
05:28 Andre: any concerns with PHI and hosted endpoints?
05:31 Liam: hosted endpoints are fine if you choose data isolation and commit to retention windows; Dedicated gives stronger isolation and is our recommended path for PHI-sensitive workloads. Private is the strongest.
05:44 Samantha: cost — can you ballpark cost for the pilot (Dedicated) versus hosted?
05:49 Jordan: ballpark wise, hosted is easiest and might be cheaper short-term, Dedicated has commit costs but better unit economics at scale. we'll include a model with sample numbers for your traffic pattern.
06:03 Andre: want to see the cost per 1k requests given our token distribution.
06:07 Liam: we'll run a spreadsheet with sample token distributions and quantization options.
06:12 Jordan: ok planned milestones recap: access and network by week 1, pilot & bench week 2, evals and tuning week 3, production roll plan week 4. do we have correct owners? jordan/priya for comms, liam for tech, cypress infra team for config.
06:30 Samantha: yes.
06:32 Maya: quick question — we sometimes use private on-prem inference for PHI; can we hybridize? like use Dedicated for public-facing and on-prem for some customers?
06:42 Liam: yes hybrid patterns are supported; smart routing can send requests based on policy, region, or customer id. there is some complexity but it's supported.
06:53 Andre: great.
06:55 Priya: any immediate blockers?
06:57 Maya: not from infra, just need the template and service account details.
06:59 Jordan: we'll send the access template and checklist.
07:02 Samantha: timeline to production after successful pilot? about 6-8 weeks?
07:07 Jordan: typical is 4-8 weeks depending on integrations and compliance needs. with Dedicated + VPC peering i'd say 4-6 weeks. Private could push that out.
07:16 Liam: want to call out metrics we'll track in console: token cost, per-route latency, error rates, and eval regressions. you'll have dashboards and tracing hooks.
07:27 Samantha: good. can you give us a demo of the console later?
07:30 Jordan: yes we'll schedule a demo - action item.
07:33 Speaker 2: (background noise)
07:37 Priya: ok i'll recap next steps: share docs, schedule SE deep dive for benchmarks, share access template, confirm pilot start date.
07:47 Jordan: any final q's?
07:50 Andre: what's the fallback if Dedicated capacity is saturated?
07:54 Liam: we have smart routing and fallbacks to compatible model variants or hosted capacity; can be configured per route. we'll show config options.
08:05 Samantha: that's helpful.
08:08 Jordan: perfect. we'll close with a quick recap of explicit next steps.
08:12 Priya: recap - Jordan to send onboarding checklist & pricing spreadsheet; Priya to share security docs; Liam to run bench; Maya to provide VPC details.
08:22 Samantha: thanks everyone, excited to get started.
08:25 Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench and console demo.
08:28 End of meeting.
